html:
Yermak Timofeyevich was a Cossack leader who began the Russian conquest of Siberia in the 1580s, in the reign of Ivan the Terrible.

The rich Stroganov merchants, who held lands on the western side of the Urals, hired Yermak and a band of a few hundred Cossacks to fight the Khanate of Sibir. In 1582 they crossed the mountains by river, defeated Khan Kuchum with their firearms and took his capital, Qashliq, on the Irtysh River.

Yermak sent furs to Moscow and the tsar sent help. But Kuchum kept fighting, and in August 1585 he ambushed Yermak's camp by night. Yermak drowned in the Irtysh trying to escape. His victory still opened the way east, and the conquest of Siberia went on without him. Russian songs and folk tales made him a hero.
